correctness.rationale: The published half-space extreme-point theorem reduces the relevant linear minimization to contiguous log-affine laws. For such a law the mean is strictly increasing and the lower-tail probability at a fixed integer threshold is strictly decreasing in the geometric parameter. Exact rational root bracketing and derivative bounds then certify the sign of the half-mass polynomial for every one of the fifteen nontrivial pairs with support length at most seven, and certify the opposite sign for the eight-point mean-six witness. The finite certificate is exhaustive after reduction rather than an extrapolative experiment.

originality.rationale: The lead paper explicitly supplies an eight-point mean-six log-affine counterexample to the one-half bound and the localization mechanism, but the inspected text does not state that support eight is minimal. Targeted semantic and web searches for the seven/eight support cutoff and equivalent truncated-geometric formulations did not locate a statement implying this exact boundary.
residual_risks: A later or poorly indexed note could contain the same seven-versus-eight cutoff despite the targeted searches; search failure is not treated as a proof of novelty.
The originality assessment is limited to the inspected sources and indexed comparisons, not an exhaustive census of all literature.

value.rationale: The lead source highlights a natural 1/2 strengthening at integer means and exhibits an eight-point failure without identifying where failure first becomes possible. Proving that every support of size at most seven still obeys 1/2 makes the example sharp in support cardinality and supplies a clean structural boundary for a standard class of discrete log-concave laws. The cutoff is motivated by the source rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
